speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) how the income gap has been trending over the past five years; (b) what are the longer-term strategic plans to narrow the income gap in a sustainable manner; and (c) how many people are in the bottom 20th percentile of household income over the past five years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In fact, this is the highest among all the deciles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Nevertheless, a job is still the best welfare, and full employment is still the best protection for our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Our efforts to narrow the income gap in a sustainable manner must, first and foremost, be based on encouraging work and levelling up the skills, productivity and wages of lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This is the reason behind the implementation of Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) and Workfare Training Support (WTS) for all lower-wage workers and, likewise, the use of policy levers to implement the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) in the cleaning, security and landscaping sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: These are our core measures to help lower-wage workers to learn new skills, take on better jobs with higher productivity and secure fairer and better wages in an inclusive, progressive and sustainable way.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In other words, in the previous five years, it was 2.1% for the 20th percentile versus 2.9% for the median.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This has narrowed to 2.9% versus 3% in the last five years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: There is, however, still much to be done.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We will continue to strengthen our support framework for lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: For example, PWM is today a ladder of minimum wage points.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We are working to transform it to become a ladder of wage ranges so as to provide more scope for wage growth for our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This will help prevent wage stagnation at the various wage points, a common challenge faced by other countries with minimum wage policies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The reason why I asked the question is because I am concerned about the general trends globally with income inequality.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am aware that, as the Minister mentioned just now, the range of policies that Singapore has undertaken, such as PWM, the transfers and also transformation of the economy and creating jobs for the future.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But there is a sustainable manner in which we want to undertake over the long term, in terms of addressing the income inequality from a longer-term strategic perspective.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is the Minister concerned about a potential risk of rising inequality from global trends that may actually impact Singapore even though we have not seen it at the moment?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the Group of 20 (G20) Labour and Employment Ministerial Meeting held last month in Beijing, one issue being discussed by the Labour Ministers from the G20 countries was the widening of income gap.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Hence, they called for not just innovation-driven, but also inclusive growth.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Page: 38 Madam, in the case of Singapore, as I mentioned, we adopted a slightly different approach.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Our approach is through WIS, WTS and PWM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: They have expressed interest in what Singapore is doing under our PWM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There is still a lot of room for us to strengthen it further.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, in the case of the cleaning sector, we are now talking about transforming the ladder of minimum wage point into a ladder of wage ranges, so that there will be more scope for our cleaners to see their wages moving up within the wage range.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is something that the Tripartite Committee on Cleaners is now working on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the case of the landscaping sector, yes, we have a PWM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But for that sector, we believe that the solution is to go for skills specialisation because in the landscaping sector, there are more skills and jobs, more equipment and technologies being introduced.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, we are not stopping at this PWM in terms of the basic framework.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Rather, we are still looking for ways to further sustain that.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Our aim is to ensure that the wage increase at the 20th percentile level in the coming years will, at least, be able to keep up with that of the median wage, if not higher.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is something that the National Trades Union Congress, the Labour Movement, has been calling for in the past few years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), we share the same commitment.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I think the employers are with us as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There is no easy way forward, but the tripartite partners, working together, must find a way to sustain the wage increase at the lower-wage worker level.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: With the early successes, we have done well with the lower-wage group.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: But I think one area is the sandwich class, that is, those in the 30th to 60th percentiles.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I think we can do more and do even better for that segment of the population.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I hope MOM, together with our tripartite partners, will be able to go full force on this, particularly with this uncertain outlook in the economy.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I would say that this concerted effort is well underway.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: F&B is a very traditional sector and has been in Singapore for a long, long time.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But if you read the plan highlighted by Deputy Prime Minister Tharman, I feel very excited.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At MOM, whenever we see an Industry Transformation Plan being announced, we move in very quickly.
